prompts.prompt: Name a way to prepare potatoes
prompts.hint: Think about the cooking method first — boiling, mashing, roasting, frying — then the dishes that build on them. Plenty of everyday answers sit at the common end, while regional preparations and less obvious styles are where the rarer, higher-value picks hide.

prompts.prompt: Name an animal whose name is exactly four letters long
prompts.hint: Four letters covers a lot of ground, from household pets to farm animals, birds, fish and reptiles. Cast wide and don't stop at the most obvious family pet; a surprising number of wild and aquatic animals fit the box perfectly.

prompts.prompt: Name someone who's won MVP (NBA/NFL/MLB), Premier League Player of the Season, or won the Ballon d'Or
prompts.hint: This spans several different honours across American sport and world football, so the answer pool is enormous. Football's biggest names sit at the crowded end, while older legends and players remembered for one dominant league season are the picks most people forget.

prompts.prompt: Name a chemical element whose symbol is one letter
prompts.hint: Only a small fixed set of chemical elements use a single-letter symbol, so this one is really a recall test. Run through the alphabet letters that can stand alone as a symbol, then choose an element that sits in the middle of the pack rather than the first guess.

prompts.prompt: Name a type of station (like a train station)
prompts.hint: A 'station' goes well beyond trains. Think about the places people work out of, the spots that keep city services running, and the platforms that broadcast or transmit. Many of these answers are everyday words that simply never get called to mind under time pressure.

prompts.prompt: Name a country whose name ends in the letter E
prompts.hint: The letter E is a common country-name ending across several continents. Start with the big European names, then push into Africa, the Americas and island nations — the less obvious geography is where the highest-value answers tend to sit.

Look beyond the two or three most famous movie teams. Comic book history is full of superteams across the big universes and beyond. A strong pick is one most casual fans recognise but rarely think to name first.

analysis: The one prompt that can genuinely trip you up is the element question: single-letter chemical symbols are a closed list, so there is nothing to reason your way into — you either remember them or you don't. Every other prompt on the page leaves the door open. 'Prepare potatoes' or 'a four-letter animal' will take almost anything sensible, which means those rounds are won by whoever reaches a slightly less obvious answer before the clock runs out, not by whoever knows more.

The MVP and Ballon d'Or line is the day's quiet trap. It looks like the friendliest question because everyone can name a superstar instantly, but those household names are exactly what the rest of the field types first. The real points tend to hide with the player remembered for one sudden, dominant season and then forgotten.

The country-ending-in-E and potato prompts end up doing the same job from opposite directions: they spread the scoring far enough that the gap comes down to how willing you are to push past the first two or three obvious answers. The superhero question, stuck in the middle, stays welcoming because casual viewers and long-time comic readers can both settle on a team without straining.
